purpose: Assesses whether the organization can detect or prevent an adversary from actively disabling, tampering with, or breaking security defenses rather than simply hiding from them.
summary: Defense Impairment (new tactic added in ATT&CK v19, split out from Defense Evasion) consists of techniques adversaries use to actively disable, weaken, or break security controls, such as disabling logging, killing security tools, tampering with EDR agents, or modifying firewall rules to lose visibility entirely rather than simply evading detection.
expectedStatementElements: How the organization detects and alerts when security tools (EDR, logging, firewall) are disabled or tampered with
What tamper-protection features are enabled on endpoint security and logging agents
How the integrity of security configuration (firewall rules, logging pipelines) is monitored for unauthorized changes
How quickly a gap in security visibility caused by defense impairment would be noticed and investigated
evidenceExamples: Tamper-protection configuration for EDR and logging agents
Alerting configuration for security tool service stoppage or configuration changes
Firewall and logging pipeline change monitoring/integrity checks
Incident or test results showing detection of a deliberately disabled security control
commonGaps: Security tools and logging agents can be disabled or uninstalled without triggering any alert
Tamper protection isn't enabled on EDR agents, allowing them to be stopped by a privileged attacker
Firewall rule or logging pipeline changes aren't monitored for integrity, so a quiet change goes unnoticed
A gap in visibility caused by a disabled security tool could persist for a long time before being noticed
interviewQuestions: If someone disabled your EDR agent right now, would you find out, and how fast?
Is tamper protection actually enabled on your endpoint security tools, or could a local admin turn it off?
Would an unauthorized firewall rule or logging change get flagged?
How long could a gap in security visibility go unnoticed in your environment?
